newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks turn higher as Fin One holds its own.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks turn higher as Fin One holds its own.

text.p: Thai stocks had shaken off their early gloom by the lunch break, posting moderate gains as bargain-hunters bought heavily discounted shares in troubled Finance One Plc and other blue chips, brokers said.
"Investors bought Finance One plus some large capitalised bank and energy issues because they thought the prices of these stocks were cheap now," said Bunsom Kesapradist of Asia Credit.
The composite SET index was up 8.02 points, or 1.44 percent, at 566.19 by the break after turnover of 1.9 billion baht.
Finance One, which resumed trading after a three-month suspension, was down 16.55 baht at 7.20 after opening at 6.00.
Finance One was suspended after news of its planned merger with Thai Danu Bank Plc, which collapsed last week.
Finance One was first-ranked on the list of most active stocks in terms of value by the lunch break.
"I think local mutual funds and retailers were active this morning. There was no fresh news to stimulate investment and they bought because stocks prices are now cheap," said Bunsom.
Bangkok Bank rose three baht to 149 while Dhana Siam advanced 1.75 to 20 and Advanced Info gained eight to 178.
